sara-eng: Noticing a repeating isolation pattern with cust-omega Dedicated VPC peering + on-prem tunnel. 3 flaps in 9 days, customers seeing resets and elevated p99 latency.

mike-sre: On it. Any recent config changes on either side or infra maintenance?

sara-eng: No internal maints during events. Customer says they upgraded router OS two weeks ago but then rolled back. Logs from last flap:```
2024-11-22T04:12:01Z peer:10.2.1.5 BGP-RESET localpref=100 reason=MTU
2024-11-22T04:12:03Z tunnel:omega-gw framg_drop pkt=1506 direction=tx
2024-11-22T04:12:04Z runtime cache evict key=kv-3ab2 cause=prefix-churn
```

ayana-ps: Customer environment: legacy edge router (firmware 7.2.1), strict maintenance window policy (only Tue/Thu 09:00-11:00 UTC). They asked us not to make changes outside that window.

kevin-eng-infra: Short-term mitigations we can propose without touching customer box: 1) drop MTU on our peering interface to 1400, 2) add a hold-time bump on the BGP session to tolerate brief flaps, 3) apply a route to steer large packets away from frag path. I can run a canary for #1 and #2.

jordan-ml: Telemetry correlation shows prefix-refresh bursts at ~72h cadence. When those refreshes align with bursts of large packets, runtime evicts hot KV entries and sessions reset. Suggest we add a pin policy to runtime to prioritize long-lived prefixes for a short window.

mike-sre: I'll own RCA and coordinate captures. Need: read-only config from cust router, syscall MTU on gateway, and pcap from tunnel endpoint. Can ayana confirm access?

ayana-ps: I'll request the Tue 09:00-11:00 UTC slot and permission for read-only access plus a one-hour elevated call. If they deny, plan B is snapshot-only + observation.

kevin-eng-infra: Canary plan: change our peering MTU to 1400 on canary-host-03 at 09:15 UTC Tuesday, monitor BGP and runtime metrics for 48h. Rollback command ready. Will paste checklist in thread before change.

mike-sre: Triage checklist I will follow: ```
1) start tcpdump on tunnel endpoint (filters: BGP, ICMP, esp)
2) `show bgp neighbors` + export routes
3) check kernel MTU/net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc
4) correlate runtime evict logs and session drops
```

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-241234-omega-peer, priority=P2, owners=[mike-sre, kevin-eng-infra], link=https://redwood/incs/INC-241234-omega-peer

sara-eng: Action items (owner - ETA):
- Customer access & slot (ayana-ps) - 2024-11-26
- Canary MTU + holdtime bump (kevin-eng-infra) - 2024-11-27 09:15 UTC
- RCA packet captures + config export (mike-sre) - 2024-11-27 12:00 UTC
- Runtime pinning eval (jordan-ml) - 2024-12-01
- Comms + runbook draft for customer (sara-eng/ayana-ps) - 2024-11-28

mike-sre: I'll post interim findings after the capture. If we see consistent fragmentation leads, we'll recommend permanent MTU alignment and an on-prem patch schedule.

kevin-eng-infra: Canary checklist (short):
- verify canary-host-03 baseline metrics
- apply MTU=1400 to peering interface
- bump bgp hold-time to 90s
- monitor BGP flaps, p99 latency, runtime-evict count for 48h
- rollback if packet loss >0.5% or new errors appear

sara-eng: We'll do daily stand at 09:00 UTC for the next 3 business days; post status in this thread each morning. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
